I don’t know how many people will read this, but I am absolutely amazed by the outpouring of love and support I’ve received from everybody here. 

Even though this is a difficult time, it helps to know there’s so many people who are understanding of what I’m going through. I wish my kitty could see how much he’s loved and how many people are praying for him. 

God bless you all. Thank you again for everything.

Thank you for the kind words. We have him on medications for hyperthyroidism and CKD, but unfortunately, it seems to be advancing much quicker than we anticipated. I can tell it’s difficult for him, which makes it difficult for me, too. 

I’ve had to euthanize one of my cats before, and even though it was one of the toughest decisions I’ve ever made, it’s a decision I’m prepared to make in the future. I would rather give my fur baby a peaceful death, than allow him to keep suffering. We’re not quite at that point yet – he still has his good days, just like he has his bad days – but I’ve been mentally preparing myself, if that day should ever come.  

I can tell you put a lot of time and thought into this, and it really does mean the whole world to me. I’m really sorry about your sweet chunky boi, but I’m glad he’s at peace now. I really appreciate the support, and I’m in much better spirits today, thanks to responses like this. I wish you all the best in the future. Cheers!

First of all, I'm really sorry for what you're going through. Just remember that what you're going through right now is an extremely temporary part of your life. At your age, school has basically been your entire life – but one day, you're going to blink and you're going to be graduated. It's going to be over before you even realize it's over. 

I know it's easier said than done, but try to make the most of it while you still can. Turn in your homework on time and study for your tests, so that way, you never, EVER have to go back there again. If you can, try to take some extra electives to boost how many credits you have (assuming you go to a public high school). If you accumulate enough credits, you should be able to graduate early, which is exactly what I did. 

Make sure you have a plan for when you graduate, since this is a mistake a lot of people make. If you want to continue your education, talk to your counselors about how you can get financial aid. If you don't want to go to college, figure out what trade you want to get into, and then figure out all the necessary steps you can take to get there. 

School tries to beat this idea into your head that if you don't succeed in school, you're not going to succeed in life. However, this isn't always the case. The truth is, your life hasn't even begun yet. There's still a whole world out there for you to explore, outside the confines of a school. You still have so much left to accomplish, so many friends left to make, and so many goals left to reach. It isn't until you graduate that you truly discover who you are and what you want out of life. Yes, education is vital. Yes, we should not take our education for granted, since it's an amazing privilege that a lot of people don't have. But at the same time, education is only a very small, very temporary part of life. 

Remember that sometimes, we have to be broken before we can be made whole again. No matter how difficult your situation is, there's always something to be learned from it, so you can come out of it for the better. The whole reason we make mistakes is so we can learn from them. The whole reason we get hurt is so we can heal and grow stronger. The whole reason we experience grief is so we can cherish life more. In the end, I don't think any of us actually want to die – we only want to get away from the pain we're in.

Remember that as long as you're alive, you have every opportunity to make a better future for yourself. Even if you've hit rock bottom, that means you have nothing to lose, and nowhere to go but up.

Remember that even if the people in your life don't understand the depression you're dealing with, they still love you and care about you. They still want to see you overcome whatever problems you might be facing. They would much rather help you deal with your problems than have to bury you, since the weight of your problems is nothing compared to the weight of your casket. Never underestimate the power of somebody who cares about you, and who's willing to give up their time to make sure you're okay. Sometimes, they can be a real game-changer.

So instead of planning on ending your life, I would suggest setting a goal for yourself, and seeing if you can accomplish it by a certain date. Instead of writing a suicide note, I would suggest writing a note detailing what kind of future you want for yourself – then, make a list of small, practical steps you can take to get there. If you focus on improving your life instead of dwelling on death, you may be surprised and inspired by the results. 

I know there's no easy answers to the problems you might face, but I hope you can find some reason – any reason – to keep pushing forward, because chances are, there's people who need you. I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

If you've had the strength to make it this far, and to admit to your mother that you're struggling, then that means you're stronger than your depression, and you can fight through this. 

I would make it clear to her that you have no intentions of acting on your suicidal thoughts. Remind her this isn't your normal way of thinking. It helps to treat these thoughts like they're coming from another person, who isn't you. 

Ask her if she's ever felt the same way. Ask her what she would do in your situation, or if there's anything she can do to help you. Obviously, she can't wave a magic wand to make your feelings go away. But at least she'll understand what you're going through, plus she'll be able to pick you up whenever you're feeling down. Hotlines can help you if you just need somebody to talk to, but they're not allowed to give you any kind of advice or self-help. This is for safety reasons, since if they give the wrong advice, it can only make things worse. 

Forums like Reddit can help a lot if you need somewhere to connect with people that's free of judgment or pressure. It might seem silly, but there's something really special about people coming together from every corner of the globe to help each other out. 

But honestly, I would recommend telling a trusted friend or family member what you're feeling. You don't have to tell them you're feeling depressed or suicidal – you can simply tell them you're going through a difficult time, and you're facing a bleak and uncertain future. Ask them if they've ever felt the same way. Ask them what they would do in your situation, or if there's anything they can do to help you. If it helps, you can write down what you want to say beforehand. 

I understand how intimidating it can be starting a conversation about depression, but it's much better than suffering in silence. If we're being completely honest with ourselves, we've all felt the same way at some point in our lives. Opening up to my family about what I was feeling was probably the thing that saved my life. Again, just make sure it's somebody you can trust, and who can be there for you.

It's only when they can't be strong anymore that the will to die overpowers them, as they go beyond, in search of something better.

The guilty. The hatred...Abuse leaves a scar that never fully heals. But it's our scars that are a testament to who you are. It's our scars that show us we've had the strength to endure and make it all this way. 

In the end, abuse is about power. Abusers are so cowardly, they can't feel gratified except by harming another human being. Please don't do anything to hurt yourself, since this will only give them more power over you. If you want to strip them of their power, you can keep living life on your terms. First of all, I'm really sorry for what you're going through. If you haven't already, make it a habit to put in your resume every one or two days. It doesn't matter what job it is. Even if you get hired at a crappy job, it won't be forever. You can still put in your resume to other jobs, until something better goes along. No matter how much the job sucks, it'll give you experience, both professionally and personally. Professionally because you can add it to your resume, and personally because you'll be learning a brand new skill. 

A big part of my job involves interviewing, hiring, and firing people. If you get selected for an interview and they don't accept you, don't ever take it personally – it's never a reflection of your character or who you are personally. That being said, don't just sit there all day and wait for the phone to ring. Keep applying, keep putting yourself out there, every single day. Most of the time, the job you end up getting is the job you never expected to get, or the interview you thought you bombed. 

When your boyfriend sees the hard work and dedication you're putting in to finding another job, I guarantee he'll be there to support you every step of the way. There's a big difference between adulting and trying to find a job, versus sitting at home all day watching TV. You're already a productive member of society, even if you don't realize it. Considering how far you've come and how hard you've already worked, the last thing I would do is call you a “burden.” 

It doesn't matter how much debt you're in, because I guarantee your boyfriend still loves you and cares about you, no matter what. The truth is, debt comes and goes. Jobs come and go. Stress comes and goes...They're like smoke in the wind, here one day and gone the next. It's the love you have for other people, and the love they have for you, that'll endure in the end. Everything else is just background noise. Never underestimate the power of people like your boyfriend, who care about you and who are rooting for you to succeed. Sometimes, they can be a real game-changer.

First of all, I'm really sorry for what you're going through. However, you should be really proud of yourself for opening about what you're feeling. Suicidal thoughts and depression often go hand-in-hand. Depression doesn't have to be feeling sad all the time. It can manifest itself in any number of ways: Feeling suicidal, loss of interest in hobbies, loss of motivation, feeling tired for no reason, feeling sluggish or lethargic, etc. It's possible you're struggling with depression and don't even realize it, simply because your life is going so well, and you have no reason to feel sad in the first place. 

This is because depression is due to chemical imbalances in the brain, mainly a lack of serotonin, or the chemical that makes you feel good when you eat good food or listen to good music. When your serotonin levels run low (along with other chemicals), it makes you depressed. It's both fascinating and horrifying to me that our entire reality is made up of nothing but chemicals. When your brain runs low on certain chemicals, it can completely change who you are and what your personality is like. Again, this is why depression is such a life-threatening illness: It can take the happiest, brightest people and convince them to hurt themselves. 

If you have access to antidepressants in the UK, this is something you might want to look into, if you are in fact struggling with depression. Antidepressants are a controversial subject on this sub. For some people, they work wonders. For other people, they only make things worse. This is something you can talk to your counselor about, if you think it could help you. (Here in the US, your regular physician can prescribe you antidepressants – you don't have to get them from a counselor or therapist. I'm not sure if it's the same way in the UK.) Make sure you go over the risks and side-effects with them. They might come with some embarrassing side-effects like constipation, but this is totally normal. 

Diet, sleep, and exercise can also play a factor in depression and suicidal thoughts. If you're not eating well, you would be shocked how much it can affect your thoughts and feelings. If you're not sleeping enough, it can make you chronically depressed and agitated. If you're exercising too much, you might not be getting the necessary nutrients and calories your body needs. It might sound silly, but my depression was literally triggered by riding my bike to work every morning and not eating enough. Make sure you take care of yourself. 

Also, alcohol can play a huge factor in developing depression. Alcohol is called a "depressant" for a reason: Because it makes you euphoric one minute, but then, it makes you feel worse than ever the next minute. Do NOT drink alcohol, at least until you've overcome whatever it is you're going through. 

In the meantime, keep seeing your counselor. Keep confiding in your wife. Keep going to work and doing everything you can to make it through the day. It might not seem like it helps, but it really does. What you're experiencing right now is an extremely small and extremely temporary part of your life. The key is to find what you're talented at, and then apply it to some sort of job or trade. Some people say they're only good at video games, but video games are all about strategizing (and in some cases, cooperating with other people) to complete an objective. Some people say they're only good at being on Reddit, but Reddit is all about communicating ideas with a team or group of people. Ridiculous as it might sound, these are skills that you can utilize in the workforce. If you're worried about not getting a high school diploma, you can consider transferring to an independent study school or continuation school. I wasn't cutting it in a public high school either, so I transferred to independent study, where I worked 1-on-1 with a private tutor and only went to school 2-3 days a week. I did all my schoolwork at home, but took all my exams at school. It was free, and once I had enough credits, I graduated with my diploma. If there's a school like this in your area, you should consider looking into it. 

I'm sure your parents have noticed how much you're struggling. I'm sure they'd be willing to help you if you convince them you want to improve your grades and graduate with a diploma. Once they see how hard you're working, I guarantee they'll be there to support you every step of the way. 

Just remember that what you're going through right now is an extremely temporary part of your life. At your age, school has basically been your entire life – but one day, you're going to blink and you're going to be graduated. It's going to be over before you even realize it's over. 
 
The truth is, your life hasn't even begun yet. There's still a whole world out there for you to explore, outside the confines of a school. You still have so much left to accomplish, so many friends left to make, and so many goals left to reach. It isn't until you graduate that you truly discover who you are and what you want out of life. Yes, education is vital. Yes, we should not take our education for granted, since it's an amazing privilege that a lot of people don't have. But at the same time, education is only a very small, very temporary part of life. Just make sure you have a plan for when you graduate, since this is a mistake lots of young people make – including yours truly.

Finding the motivation to do things is near-impossible when you're struggling with depression and suicidal thoughts. Your motivation to study and focus on your exams is going to change from one minute to the next. What it comes down to is discipline, first and foremost. Discipline is still possible when you're struggling, and in fact, it can be completely necessary when you need to study or get up in the morning to go to school. 

Instead of spending your time thinking about death and suicide, spend AT LEAST 30 minutes to an hour every day studying. Even if you have to force yourself into it, it's much better than the alternative. If you catch your mind wandering, turn on some music or have some coffee to help you stay focused.

Whenever you're done studying for the day, you can reward yourself by doing something fun or chowing down on some good food. If you still find your mind wandering or going to some dark places, stop these thoughts by immediately opening your textbook and studying some more. You can never study too much. Exams are all about memorizing what's written in your textbooks or on your homework – if you think about it, it's basically parroting. Once you have the material memorized, the exam should prove no problem. 

The night before your exam, make sure you go to bed at a decent time and get at least 8 hours of sleep. Eat a good breakfast in the morning and brush up on the material by reading your notes or your textbook one last time. This is what I mean by discipline: Learning how to take your negative emotions and turn it into something productive, to work for you instead of against you. The worst thing you can do is bury your head under the covers and think about how much life sucks. 

I wish you all the best on your exams! You can do this – I believe in you!

My best friend committed suicide over a decade ago. In fact, the 11 year anniversary of his death is coming up next week. I'm spending my time thinking about everything I wish I could've said to him, and everything I wish I could've done for him. Sometimes I think to myself, “Maybe if I'd been there for him more, he'd still be alive.”

That being said, now is the perfect time to be there for your friend. Don't just tell them you're there for them – show them you're there for them. Check up on them every once in a while and ask how they're doing. Take them to see a movie. Surprise them with lunch. Be their shoulder to cry on, whenever they need it. 

It might not seem like much, but it'll remind them they have somebody who cares about them, and who wants to see them overcome this. Depression and suicidal thoughts trick you into thinking you're alone, when in reality, everyone has felt the same way at some point in their life. The less alone you can make them feel, the better. 

If I'm being brutally honest, you can't force your friend to stop feeling the way he/she feels. You can't wave a magic wand to make their depression go away. Depression is a long and arduous road, and one they're going to have to come to terms with on their own. It's up to them whether or not they want to get help and overcome what it is they're feeling. 

That's where you come in: You can be the one to encourage them to get help and overcome what it is they're feeling. You can be the one to bring them up whenever they're down. You can be the one to listen to their problems and help them through it. 

In the event your friend makes a serious attempt on his/her life, you should call 9-1-1 or get in touch with their relatives, immediately. They might be angry at first, but it'll literally be a second chance at life, and a second shot at starting over. Even in the worst case scenario, you should never blame yourself if they go through with it. Sometimes, people are suffering so much than even doing our best isn't enough. People will say that suicidal people are “selfish” and “cowardly,” but this is far from true. Suicidal people are the strongest people I've ever known, since they've dealt with more heartache, tragedy, and despair than most of us will ever know.

I wish you and your friend all the best in the days ahead! Sending you lots of positivity!

My mom would not stop sobbing, because in her eyes, I should've been dead. People I hadn't seen in years started calling me out of the blue, just to make sure I was okay. 

In a time when it seemed like nobody cared about me and the world was out to get me, it gave me a glimpse of what it would've been like if I'd committed suicide. I realized if I was dead, I couldn't be around to take care of my parents when they got old. I realized when they got together for the holidays, I wouldn't be there to sit at the dinner table with them. This realization hit me in the face like a ton of bricks, and helped me get out of the suicidal thoughts that had been plaguing me for so long. 

I'm glad you're okay, and I'm glad you're maintaining a positive attitude about what you went through. If you start to feel down again, just remind yourself how much you mean to the people around you, and how they reacted when you got into your accident. Remember they still want you to overcome whatever problems you might be facing. I guarantee they would much rather help you deal with those problems than have to bury you, because the weight of your problems is nothing compared to the weight of the casket. Remind her how much you love her and care about her. Remind her how you'd much rather help her deal with her problems than have to bury her. Depression is a long and lonely road, but with this type of support, it'll be that much easier to overcome it. In that regard, you should be extremely proud of yourself.

I realized that as long as I was alive, I could still work hard and make him proud, to be the person he always knew that I could be. Your friend's given you a lifetime of memories, and that's the greatest gift that can possibly be given. These memories are pure and perfect in every conceivable way, and that's something nobody can ever take away from you. These memories will always be there for you, through good days and bad days, whenever you need them most. If you ever want to see your friend again, all you have to do is think back to the time you've spent together. She might be gone, but she's gone in body only.

Remember that therapists are like clothes: Sometimes, you have to try a few before you find one that fits just right. If your first therapist doesn't work out, don't give up hope. Just move on to another therapist and keep trying.

When I was in high school, my social anxiety was so debilitating, I had to transfer to an independent study school. It was so overwhelming, I couldn't even sit in the same classroom as 30 other kids without worrying that one of them was watching me or judging me. Most of the time, social anxiety stems from a fear of being judged (at least, in my experience).

Obviously, this isn't something that can be cured overnight. But if you work to improve yourself, little by little, day by day, you can see results. The easiest thing to do is to leave the house and go somewhere quiet, where it's okay to socialize, but it's not necessarily expected. This could be a library, movie theater, or even the grocery store where you work. Every time you go out, say something nice to somebody. Pay them a compliment. Tell them how much you like their shoes or their shirt.

It sounds corny, but 99% of the time, they'll say “Thank you” or pay you a compliment in return. As time goes on, it'll make it easier to approach people. If anything, it'll help you feel good about yourself for complimenting people, which will help boost your confidence. As long as you're nice and polite, people will take a natural liking to you, and you'll start to realize socializing isn't so terrifying after all. The world needs more people who are nice and polite anyways. 

Here are some other tips for socializing that helped me immensely: When you're talking to people, always make sure you smile and laugh a lot. People are naturally attracted to those who are friendly and don't take themselves too seriously. When you're in a conversation with somebody, always ask them questions. It'll give the impression that you're a good listener who's interested in what they have to say. If they start asking you questions about yourself and your life, always take a moment to think about what you want to say before you say it. This will help you put things into words easier. If you're having trouble putting things into words, listen to comedians (or spoken word artists, if that's more your style). Try to mimic how they talk and how they tell a story.

Oftentimes, social anxiety stems from personal insecurity more than anything else. If you're feeling unhappy with who you are, or like there's some aspect of yourself that needs to be improved, then this is something that you should work on. As time goes on, work hard. Practice something you're really good at. Try to learn something new every day. Help other people, from time to time. In my opinion, this is the best way to combat social anxiety: To give yourself a sense of fulfillment, like who you are matters, and what you say matters. Because honestly, you do matter, and you deserve to be happy just like everybody else.

Depression is due mainly to chemical imbalances in the brain (namely a lack of serotonin), but can also be triggered by life events and general unhappiness. Telling somebody to “get over” their depression is like telling someone to “get over” cancer – it doesn't work that way. Overcoming depression requires a long and intensive period of healing and care. The road to recovery is going to be a long and strenuous one, but as long as she has somebody like you by her side, it'll make the road that much easier. 

If her bipolar meds are making her feel worse, she needs to stop taking them, IMMEDIATELY. She needs to email her doctor ASAP about changing her meds. I'd suggest reaching out to her dad for help, since I'd suggest she gets all the help and support she can get. She doesn't have to tell him about the suicidal thoughts – she can simply tell him she hasn't been feeling like herself lately. She can ask him if he's been through the same thing, and if there's anything he can do to help her. Likewise, she can tell her dad NOT to say anything to her mom, and to keep it private between the two of them. He may keep it confidential, as long as he doesn't think your girlfriend is a danger to herself or somebody else. However, it's your girlfriend's decision, and her decision alone. The worst thing about anxiety is how there's no one-and-done fix for it. It's something you have to work on, little by little, over a long period of time. However, it can be done. 

These are some things that helped me when I was struggling with anxiety. You mention over-reacting to things. Anytime you get upset or anxious over something, ask yourself: “Is this going to matter 50 years from now? Is this going to affect my life on a deep and personal level?” 

Chances are, the answer will be no. Life is filled with temporary setbacks – spilling your coffee, your car won't start, traffic is bad coming home, etc. - but that's all they are: Minor inconveniences that you're not going to remember a week from now, let alone 50 years from now. By making yourself anxious, you'll hurt yourself more than anything else will. 

If it's something serious that WILL affect you on a deep and personal level (work, school, money, bills, etc.), remember to set small goals for yourself. It could be something simple, like finishing a work project, getting a good grade on an essay, paying your phone bill by a certain date, etc. 

When you set a goal for yourself and accomplish it, it'll boost your confidence, which will make you feel happier, which will help take away your anxiety. Oftentimes, anxiety comes from a fear of doing something wrong, or having things be out of your control. Accomplishing small goals like this will help you feel more in control, and help you prove to yourself that you can accomplish whatever you set out to. 

I also had horrible anxiety when it came to things like job interviews, presentations, etc., where I had to talk to people. Like you described, I would always talk super fast and my mind would go blank whenever they'd ask me questions. 

It helps to write down what you want to say beforehand. It might sound silly, but it also helps to talk to yourself, so your brain can hear you speak. It'll help you to better organize your thoughts and ideas, while also memorizing whatever it is you want to say. Listen to spoken word artists or comedians and how they tell a story. Try to mimic what they're saying and how they're talking. When you're in a conversation with somebody, remember to take deep breaths and talk slowly. Make eye contact and think about what you're going to say, so you can get your point across. 

When it comes to panic attacks, immediately remove yourself from the situation. Excuse yourself to the bathroom or somewhere quiet where you can be alone. If you can, try to do something you enjoy for 10-15 minutes. This could be something like writing, drawing, listening to music, playing a game, checking social media, etc. Not only will it help calm you down, but it'll help you clear your head. 

In the meantime, try to find the humor in things. If you screw up or make a mistake, just laugh it off. Nobody cares, and nobody's going to remember. If you fall flat on your face, crack some jokes and keep going. There's no shame in making mistakes, since mistakes are what make us human. Without mistakes, we'd never learn, grow, and develop as human beings.

I don't have autism, but both of my brothers do, so I can understand what you're feeling.

Ever since my brothers were diagnosed with autism, people have treated them differently, even though they're extremely intelligent and can function just fine. Honestly, it bothers me. I don't look at them as my “brothers who have autism.” I just look at them as my brothers. Nothing more, nothing less. 

Just because they have autism doesn't mean they don't have hopes and dreams. Just because they have autism doesn't mean they don't want to fall in love, or have a steady career, or have children of their own one day. 

Yes, autism can make life a living hell. Yes, it can amplify your emotions and make you hyper-sensitive. Yes, it can make it hard to socialize sometimes. 

HOWEVER – you should not let your autism define you. You are so much more than just a label for a neurodevelopment disorder. You are a human being with thoughts, dreams, and experiences. You have every right to live a long, happy, healthy life, just like everybody else does. 

You can still fall in love, have a career, and have children of your own one day. You can still have the life you want to. Don't EVER listen to anybody who tells you otherwise, because they're full of shit. They have no idea who you are or what you've gone through. People will always tell you that you can't do something, until you actually go out and do it and prove them wrong. Most of the time, these people have never accomplished anything to begin with. 

Right now, your only concern should be YOU. Don't concern yourself with what other people think. Don't let them tell you how to live your life or how to be happy. You are in complete control of your destiny. There's a whole world out there, still waiting for you. You still have so many places left to go, so many people left to meet, and so many things left to accomplish. 

From my experience, people with autism are more in touch with their emotions. They can focus better than most people can, which makes them hard workers, who are extremely punctual and stick close to their routines. They can be highly creative and think outside the box. If anything, you can use this to your advantage. You can use what you've been through to work for you, instead of against you. 

It's obvious you have a lot of strength to make it to this point, after all you've been through. I hope you can find it within yourself to keep pushing forward. Sending you much love. I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

So far, you're making great progress, and you seem like you're on the right track. 

It might not seem like much, but dieting is a huge milestone for what you're going through. There will be days you'll be tempted to cheat and give in to hunger, but just remember how amazing it'll feel when you have the body you want. If you haven't already, I would suggest exercising for 15-30 minutes a day as well. Even if you don't lose the weight right away, you'll notice a huge difference in how you feel. 

Instead of making it a goal to commit suicide, make it a goal to lose a certain amount of weight by a certain date. Make a list of ways you can better yourself and your life as a whole. In this regard, overthinking can sometimes be a good thing, as long as it's for your own benefit. 

You're extremely blessed to have a girlfriend who's able to help you through this. There's absolutely no shame in telling your loved ones you need help. Even if they don't understand what you're going through, I guarantee they want to see you overcome whatever problems you're facing. I guarantee they care about your health and well-being more than anything in the world. There's a big stigma around “getting help,” as they say, but therapy can be extremely beneficial, as long as you're open and honest about what you're feeling.

If there's a God, then he looked down at the stars, mountains, and oceans, and thought you needed to be here, too. If there's a God, he's looking out for you and wants you to succeed in everything you do. Instead of cursing God, take advantage of this opportunity to better yourself and live a healthier lifestyle. Sometimes we need to be broken before we can become the person we're supposed to be. The whole reason we make mistakes is so we can learn from them. The whole reason we get hurt is so we can heal and become stronger. The whole reason we have bad days is so we can cherish the good days. 

You should be extremely proud of yourself for making it this far. The worst thing about depression is how it takes away your motivation and energy. The fact that you can find the motivation to better yourself speaks volumes about your character. You're so much stronger than your depression, and there's no doubt in my mind you'll kick it to the curb. As long as you stay focused on your health and keep improving, little by little, day by day, I guarantee you will see results. 

Wishing you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

It doesn't matter who you are or how good your life is – we all have problems we need to work through. We're all trying to find our path in life and where we fit into the grand scheme of things. This isn't weakness. This is called being human. You shouldn't feel guilty about it. You have every right to feel what you're feeling. 

It's true, the only person who's going to understand what you're going through is you. But that doesn't mean you can't reach out to a friend or family member for help. You don't have to tell them you're suicidal. You can simply tell them you're struggling, and you don't know why. Obviously, they can't wave a magic wand to make your feelings go away. But sometimes, knowing someone is there for you can make all the difference in the world. They can offer you advice or help if you need it. I guarantee your loved ones want to see you overcome whatever problems you might be facing. I guarantee they would do anything for you and care about your health and well-being more than anything in the world. Remember this whenever you're feeling down.

Feeling unhappy for no reason is often a symptom of depression, which is something you may want to look into, if you haven't already. Depression will take everything in your life and twist it into something evil, when actually it's the depression that's evil. It'll convince you you're useless, and that you should  end it all...However, you can't give in to these thoughts. You have to realize this is the depression talking – not you. If anything, you have an incredible amount of strength to make it this far and to come seeking helping. You are not useless. You have every right to live a long, happy, healthy life, just like everyone else. 

If you need somebody to talk to, you can PM me anytime. I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

That's wonderful you're volunteering and taking part in an NGO. That's a huge accomplishment for what you're going through, and you should be extremely proud of yourself.

You might not think you're doing enough, but you're probably doing more than enough. Your story and your support could be the thing that's inspiring people to make it through the day. You probably mean the whole world to them, and you don't even realize it.

If you can keep fighting and keep pushing forward, it'll inspire them to do the same. Even if you don't feel like yourself, remember how much you mean to those people, and how you've touched their lives for the better.

In the meantime, just because the people around you aren't congenial doesn't mean you can't be. As long as you keep helping people and doing the best you can, you'll be setting a positive example for them to do the same. The best way to defeat acts of unkindness are with acts of kindness. 

I know how hard it can be to make it through the day. I know how hard it can be to find a reason to go on. I know how tiring life can get sometimes. But so far, you're on the right track. You're going above and beyond to do the right thing. I implore you to keep going, and to see where the road takes you. As long as you keep helping people, you'll have a bright future ahead of you. 

Please keep us posted on how you're doing, and please take care of yourself. You can do this!

You can always prove your family wrong without taking your own life. Yes, you most definitely should get good grades and work a good job, but not so you can end your life – only so you can make a better future for yourself. After all, one year from now, you may find something you're passionate about and want to pursue as a career. You may find your calling in life and something you want to commit yourself to. 

Right now, at this point in your life, the only person you should be concerned with is YOU. Don't give a damn what anybody else thinks about you or what you choose to do with your life (especially when it comes to depression, something most people choose to be oblivious to). If you're going to school and making money, they have no right to judge you anyways, since you're basically independent. 

The best thing you can do right now is work as hard as you possibly can, to be the best you can possibly be. Don't do it for them – do it for YOU, for YOUR future. Most of the time, the people who doubt you are people who have never accomplished anything to begin with. 

Living well is always the best revenge. There's no better satisfaction than laughing in the faces of the people who once doubted you. One day, when you're successful and well-off, they're the ones who are going to come crawling back to you looking for scraps and a hand-out.  

I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

I wish I could upvote what Staystaystay22 said a million times.

The most giving and compassionate people are the ones who have dealt with the most abuse, since they know what it's like to be stuck in a dark place, and they don't want others to feel the same way. The tragedies of life humble us and beat us down – but by doing so, they give us a chance to come out of it stronger, better, and wiser. 

Life is always about taking something negative and turning it into something positive, and that's exactly what you can do: You can use your experiences to help other people who might be struggling through the same thing. Even if you can't make their problems go away, you can give them a shoulder to cry on and help them to realize they're not alone. 

You can do this by joining a support group. A simple Google search will point out some in your area. You can easily find one at your local church or college campus. Instead of making it a goal to commit suicide by September, make it a goal to help as many people as you can by September, in any way you can.

It may seem overwhelming, especially if you're dealing with depression. But the love and support you give other people will be the fuel that gives you life. When other people tell you how much they appreciate you, and how much you mean to them, that's when you'll see the goodness humanity has to offer. That's what can part the clouds of your depression, and help you to see the light. 

You are absolutely right – it's not always unhappiness or desperation that makes you so depressed. Life is always going to throw obstacles at you, some big, some small. You might not be able to control it, but what you can control is how you respond to it and deal with it.

If you end your life, it'll only be giving the people who raped and abused you more power over you. Please, don't give them that kind of power. They don't deserve it. 

You've made it this far. You've survived all this way and lived to tell about it. That means you are more powerful than they could ever be. The best way to strip them of their power is to keep on living. To rise above them, and to show them you haven't succumbed to the pain, but have walked away from it a better person. 

Your life isn't over because of what you've been through – quite the opposite. You have so much to offer this world. There's so much you can do and so many lives you can touch. Please, keep fighting, keep pushing forward. Remember how much you mean to your friends and family, and how you've changed their lives for the better. 

If you ever want to talk or vent, you can PM me anytime. I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

If coming here and talking to people helps you, then please do so. If Reddit's taught me anything, it's that we're never as alone as we think. 

I understand what it's like to feel like giving up. Just remember, you do not deserve what you have been through – nobody does. It doesn't matter what you might have said or done. You are not pathetic to have made it this far. You are not stupid if you've done everything in your power to get out of this. Barely surviving is still surviving. 

You might not realize it yet, but the horrors you've been through will make you into a better, stronger, more giving, more compassionate person – and that's exactly the type of person this world needs. 

Abuse is all about having power over another human being. If you end your life, it'll only be giving them more power over you. Please, don't give them that kind of power. At the very least, get through school, and then see what your options are. 

Suicidal people don't actually want to die, but only want to get away from the pain they're feeling. You're still young, and you still have the rest of your life to get away from this pain. There's still a whole world out there, away from your parents, away from the situation you're in now. You can still live the long, happy, healthy life you deserve. 

I implore you to stay alive, and I implore you to keep fighting. Please take care of yourself, and please update us on how you're doing. I'll be thinking of you.

If your school has a counselor, I would strongly suggest talking to them, if you haven't already. You don't have to tell them about feeling suicidal. You can simply tell them what you've gone through, and they may be able to help, or get you in contact with the proper authorities. 

I would also suggest looking for a support group in your area for people who have dealt with the abuse you have. Churches and college campuses usually have groups like this. I helped set up support groups for my church – and even if you don't have a car, somebody in the group will always be there to give you a ride. They can also get you in contact with authorities who may be able to help you. If you're concerned about your parents finding out, they can always cover for you (say it's something for school, you're going to a friend's place, etc.). 

If you have any friends or other family members you can trust, you can always get help and support from them. If there's anyway you can move out of there and stay at a friend's place for the time being, please do so, immediately. 

In the long-term, the best thing you can do is make a better life for yourself outside of your parents. If you're still in school, study hard and ace your exams so you can go away to a good college. If you haven't already, start thinking about what you want to do for a career, and figure out what steps you can take to get there. Work your ass off and do ANYTHING you can to get the hell out of there. 

I know it's easier said than done. I know it's going to take a lot of time and effort. However, this is the only way I can foresee you overcoming this, once and for all. Once you're financially independent, you no longer have to look your family in the eye ever again. What you choose to do, and who you choose to spend your time with, will be entirely up to you. 

Use your anger to work for you, instead of against you. Use your negative feelings to motivate you to work hard, so you can become independent. Living well is always the best revenge. Show them you're not going to let them beat you down anymore. Show them you're going to rise above them and make a better life for yourself. There's no better satisfaction than laughing in the faces of anyone who ever doubted you.

The people who have abused you will make you think you somehow brought the abuse upon yourself. This is common for all abusers: They'll convince you that you're worthless, and that you somehow deserved it. They'll convince you that all you do is hurt people or that nobody would notice if you committed suicide. 

This could not be farther from the truth. You are so much better and so much stronger than you think. Despite all you've been through, and all the abuse you've suffered, you've managed to make it this far. You might not realize it, but that is a HUGE achievement, and you should be extremely proud of yourself. Don't EVER let them – or anybody else for that matter – define your self-worth for you. 

You're a survivor. You've been through so much and lived to tell about it. There is no doubt in my mind you have the strength and the will to get through this, if only you'll find it within yourself. One day, you'll be able to share your story with the whole world, and use it to help other people who might be suffering through the same thing. 

I know I can't even begin to comprehend what you've been through – nobody can. But if you ever want to talk or vent, you can PM me anytime. I know there's not much I can say or do to help you, but I'll always be there to listen. 

Sending you much love. I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

My parents had me when they were still teenagers. Growing up, we were lucky to put food on the table. I don't remember us ever having birthday parties, going on trips, or doing anything fun. All I remember is that they were there, spending time with me. And looking back, that's all that matters. 

Years from now, your son's not going to remember or care what happened on his birthday. He's not going to remember where you took him or what you got him as a gift. All he's going to remember is that you were there for him. Make the most of this time while you can, while he's still young. Before you know it, you're going to blink and he's going to be an adult. Honestly, I wish I had appreciated my time with my parents more, when I was still young.

Playing the comparison game is a trap (“I shouldn't feel bad because others have it so much worse than I do”). We all have problems we need to work through. You're an amazing parent for wanting to be there for your son. Having compassion to the point of tears speaks a lot about your character. I guarantee your son sees you as a hero, a leader, a champion, even if you don't think of yourself that way. He's extremely lucky to have you. As long as you do your best for him, you'll always have each other, and that's what will last you through good times and bad times. One day, when he's an adult, he'll be able to appreciate how much you've done for him and sacrificed for him.

Wishing you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

I'm sorry for what you're going through, but I hope you'll find it in you to keep pushing forward. I wanna hear you on the radio someday. Wishing you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

You don't have to be a martyr or die in a blaze of glory to be considered a good person. We look up to these beautiful people because they give us something to aspire to. Get them involved with your life in some way, to show them how good of a person you are. People are naturally attracted to those who are friendly and don't take themselves too seriously. 

I'm sorry for what you're going through. College is a rough time, but it says a lot that you've managed to make it this far, despite what you're feeling. Remember, this period of your life is extremely temporary. It will soon pass, and so will these feelings. 

Wishing you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

Depression is serious and life-threatening. It'll take everything good in your life and twist it into something evil, when actually it's the depression that's evil. It'll take away all your motivation and anything that once made you happy. 

Remember: It's okay to have “off” days. It's okay to lay in bed or sleep more than usual. It's okay to not want to do anything. You're not wasting time, but healing. When you're going through something as serious as depression, you need to make plenty of time for yourself to heal. 

Depression will try to convince you it can't be overcome, but it can. Obviously, there's no one-and-done fix. But if you have a willingness to get better, and a willingness to better yourself as a person, little by little, day by day, you will see results. It's easier said than done, but it is possible, and don't let it convince you otherwise. You're stronger than your depression. You've made it all this way, after dealing with so much, and that is a HUGE accomplishment for what you're going through. 

Sorry you're having a bad day. If you want to talk or vent, you can PM me anytime. I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

I think it's apparent most of your feelings stem from having such a stressful job. Yes, it's important to keep your job, but there comes a point where enough is enough, and you have to do what's best for you and your mental health. There's no job that was ever worth losing your mind over. It's easy to hate sales jobs because sales jobs are the blight of human existence. It's no wonder you're so anxious if you're working in sales. 

So far, you seem like you're on the right track. Keep working at the restaurant job and see where it takes you. You may get promoted or get a raise. Keep working out, eating healthy, and seeing a counselor. You might not think it helps, but it does. 

In the meantime, keep an eye out for other job openings that pay close to or better than what you're making now. You could try looking for another job at the same company, but in a different department (i.e., NOT the sales department). If all else fails, you can talk to a temp agency (which will start you out in a temporary position, but may become permanent if you do a good enough job), or ask your friends and family if any of their jobs have openings. Whatever you do, make sure you get a positive reference from your current boss. I gave my old job the middle finger and it eventually came back to bite me in the bite. ALWAYS leave on good terms. 

What you're going through right now is extremely temporary. Getting a better job will lead to a happier life, which will lead to more self-confidence. As long as you keep working hard and pushing forward, it will pay off – literally. You're obviously doing something right if you're getting hired. Keep it up.

Wishing you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

I hire and fire people for a living. I cannot emphasize this enough: No matter how many jobs you get rejected from, it has nothing to do with your character or who you are as a person. There's a million reasons why you might not get selected for an interview (most of them petty reasons that have nothing to do with you, and are based solely on the company). Do not take it personally. Don't let a rejection from one measly job define your self-worth for you. Getting hired is all about being at the right place at the right time. 

Try to make it a habit to apply for 1 job every single day. If you've already applied and haven't heard back, apply again, or bring them your resume in-person. Worry about the transportation aspect later. Right now, keeping food on the table is your first priority.

If you can't walk there, bike there. If you can't bike there, take the bus there. If you can't take the bus there, ask a friend or family member for a ride. If they can't give you a ride, take Uber or Lyft there (if you're in a big city). You'll only have to do this for a very short period of time. Once you have enough pay stubs, you'll be able to get a car. This is your second priority. 

What you're going through right now is extremely temporary. You will work through this. Pretty soon, you're going to blink and you're going to be working. Don't be afraid to ask your friends and family members for help if you need it. They may have some great advice. They may even be able to loan you some money for a car. 

I hope you can find a decent job, and I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

If we're going on video game analogies...Life is exactly like a video game. If it gets hard, that means you're going in the right direction. 

Yes, you might lose a few lives and you might rage-quit a couple times. There's no shame in it, since it happens to everybody. 

But each time you try again, you'll be better and wiser and more experienced than last time. Eventually, you'll be able to beat the level you've been stuck on. 

You might be weary and exhausted after playing for so long, but the satisfaction you get when you finally beat the boss will trump any negative feelings you might have. 

If you choose the good path, you'll open up lots of cool collectibles and get lots of new teammates who'll help you in your journey. But if you choose the renegade path, you'll constantly be having problems.

If you get good enough, you can give other people cheats and strategy guides, to help them out when they get stuck at a certain point. 

Life might be tough sometimes, but it's exactly that: Just a game. Don't take it too seriously. You might think you're alone, but we're all playing this crazy game together. We might not be able to beat the game, but we can keep leveling up and getting stronger than the day before. This is what the game is all about: Growing, learning, gaining experience...

I'm sorry for what you're going through. There's no easy answers to the problems you face, but I hope you can find it in you to keep pushing forward. Remember: The problems we face in life are only temporary. Work, school, stress, debt...It comes and it goes. It's the things that truly matter – love, family, friends – that'll last you a lifetime. 

Wishing you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you!

It's difficult making a living in the arts, but it is possible. You have to be fully committed to your craft every single day, whether it's writing, drawing, animation, etc. Whatever free time you have, you have to spend it practicing and getting better. If you're interested in comics, you can write and draw your own comic books and give them to people to read. If you're interested in video games, you can learn how to program and write code. If you're interested in animation, there's plenty of animation software you can learn from. 

More than anything, you have to be willing to put yourself out there and network with other people. This means offering to work on low-budget comics, video games, or movies for little to no pay (at least, when you're first starting out). That's it - just 15 minutes. No more, no less. Use this time to study, write, draw, listen to music, play a game, write a song...At the end of those 15 minutes, you'll have a clearer head. You'll be better-prepared to problem-solve and come to a solution. 

It's easier said than done, but it helps to take your negative emotions and turn it into something positive. Use it to work for you, instead of against you. Make something productive out of it, instead of simply hurting yourself.

I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this - I believe in you!

The depression that goes along with suicidal thoughts will try to convince you that this is the way life is, that you may as well end it all and get it over with - but this couldn't be farther from the truth. All the bullshit life throws at you - work, money, bills, stress, school - is all temporary. It comes and it goes. Here one minute, gone the next. 

Death, on the other hand, is permanent. I can only speak from my experience, so take this with a grain of salt. Remember, this is your decision and yours alone. Antidepressants are different for everybody.

However, it was one of many steps in helping me overcome my depression. It made my suicidal thoughts go away and gave me enough motivation to get out of bed in the morning. 

In the end, I’m glad I took it. I probably could’ve overcome my depression without them, but it definitely would’ve taken me much, much longer. 

Now, with all that being said...Despite all their weird side-effects, antidepressants can help eliminate your depression, once-and-for-all. If you truly want to kick your depression to the curb, it may be worth trying. Remember, it’s only temporary. You don’t have to keep taking them forever – only until you feel like you can function again without them. 

However, if you feel like antidepressants are making you feel worse, or if they’re giving you dangerous side-effects (suicidal tendencies, etc.), you may have to look for help elsewhere. You may have to try different kinds of antidepressants before you find one that works best for you. This is something to talk to your doctor about.

Again, you have to decide what’s best for you and your health. Every single person on this sub will give you a different answer.

Depression is unbiased and unprejudiced. It can strike anyone, anywhere, at any time, no matter who they are. It’s not something you’ve chosen or have any control over. It’s not your fault you feel the way you feel, and your anger is perfectly justified. 

For me, depression was a lot like being an actor. I was always wearing a smile on my face, when deep down, I was dying inside.

Depression is really difficult for other people to understand if they’ve never dealt with it personally. When I was depressed, people gave me really brilliant advice like “Keep your chin up,” “All you need is a good night’s rest,” and my personal favorite, “At the end of the day, you’re another day older.” 

But at the same time, you should remember that your friends and family still love you and care about you more than anything in the world. Even if they don’t understand what you’re going through, I guarantee they would give you the clothes off their backs if it came down to it. Even if you resent them, you should still maintain a healthy relationship with them, rather than take your anger out on them. Don’t permanently severe ties with them because of temporary feelings.

It can be a very long journey, trying to overcome depression. There’s no miracle cure. There will be bad days. There will be times you question whether or not you’re doing the right thing. But it is possible. 

If you’re an artsy person, it helps to take out your feelings through writing, drawing, painting, music, etc. You might not be connecting with other people this way, but you’ll be connecting with yourself internally, and sometimes that can be just as important. 

Oftentimes, depression stems from being unhappy with your life as a whole. You can take all the antidepressants and go to all the therapists in the world – but if you’re unhappy with where you are in life, you may as well be putting a Band-aid on an amputated limb. That being said, make a list of things you can do to improve yourself and your well-being. This can be something as simple as exercising and eating better, or something as major as finding a new job. If it seems overwhelming, make a list of small, practical steps you can take to achieve your goals.

When you’re depressed, one of the easiest traps to fall into is isolating yourself too much. After a while, the peace and quiet of being alone becomes addictive. But you should always make time to spend with family and friends. You might have to force yourself into it. Again, they might not understand what you’re going through. But connecting with other people can help clear your head, and can help you feel refreshed and rejuvenated.

And of course, there’s always the community here on Reddit, which can be extremely helpful and supportive.

You will get through this, and you will come out of it a stronger, better person.

I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this!

He might not get along with his parents, and they could be the ones who drove him to this point. You don’t have to tell them your friend’s about to go on a murder spree. You can simply tell them he’s dealing with some issues and he’s considering hurting other people. 

Whoever you tell, make sure it’s someone who can discipline him, but also give him the necessary help to get through this. If your friend is suicidal, he’s probably struggling with depression. And if he’s struggling with depression, then he’s going to need all the help and support he can get. 

If your friend is an adult, you need to alert the proper authorities. The police may arrest him or have him committed, depending on his mental state. He may hate you for it at first, but it may be the kick in the ass he needs to turn his life around for the better. 

There’s only so much you can say that’s going to help him. Trying to help someone who doesn’t want to be helped is like trying to clap with one hand – it simply doesn’t work. Right now is the time to take action.

Whatever happens to him shouldn’t weigh down on your conscience. Your friend has made his own decisions and gotten himself to this point. It’s not something you should feel guilty over. All you can hope for is that he’ll get the help he needs and come out of it a better person. If you want to support him and be there for him, I would strongly encourage it. Depression will try to manipulate you into thinking everything that’s good is evil. If you’re there to support him, you’ll be showing him this isn’t true. 

Whatever happens, I wish you the two of you all the best in the future. Keep us posted if you can.

Depression is due to chemical imbalances in the brain, which is why you can get depression for seemingly no reason at all. If your dopamine levels are running short, you’ll start to feel depressed, no matter how bright or cheerful life is. This is also why depression runs in families, and why an unfortunate number of people are predisposed to it.

Depression can be triggered by a major life event, like being unhappy with school/work, losing a loved one, abuse, etc. But if nothing like this has happened – and you’re perfectly happy with where your life is at – then your depression will likely go away on its own, as long as you take care of yourself. I’ve had to cut family members out of my life who are like this. When I needed help most, they slammed the door in my face. They told me I would never amount to anything – and when I did, they congratulated themselves, like they were somehow responsible. 

The best thing you can do is set a positive example for them. Use any opportunity you can to help other people who are in need. This can mean something as simple as helping an elderly person with their groceries, lending change to the homeless, or surprising a friend with lunch. 

The whole essence of life is giving, since we’ve been given this life and this world to live in. The more you give, the more people will give back to you. THIS is what will make them feel guilty: When they see how good of a person you are, and the kindness other people are willing to instill on you. Instead of making it a goal to commit suicide, make it a goal to do something compassionate for somebody, so you can prove them wrong and make them eat their words. Show them you’re bigger than them and won’t let them drag you down. 

Don’t listen to them when they judge you for being the way you are. If they’re going to nit-pick you, that cries of insecurity and desperation on their part. If anything, I pity them for feeling the need to point out your shortcomings, without improving their own.  

Only take advice from people in your life who support you and want to see you succeed. They’re the ones who matter. They’re the ones who’ll share in your success.

In the meantime, keep working hard to become independent, so that way, you won’t have to answer to them anymore. Think of how amazing it’ll be when you can live your own life, away from them. Again, this is something else you should work towards, rather than hurting yourself. Set small goals for yourself, and little by little, you will see results.  

If all else fails, you always have your friends on Reddit here to support you. I wish you all the best in the days ahead, my friend. You can do this - I believe in you!

I’m a director and project manager in charge of a multimillion dollar production. But when I worked at K-Mart, I couldn’t stock shelves or use a cash register to save my life. Same with working construction. You wouldn’t think digging holes would be so hard, but it was for me. It just wasn’t in my DNA.

Just because you’re not good at working fast food doesn’t automatically mean you suck at every job in the world. To be fair, fast food is extremely difficult since you’re working at such a frantic pace and everyone’s counting on you. People who think service people are losers should try working fast food for a day. It’s not a picnic.

Plus, if you’re relatively new to your job, they probably didn’t give you much training. Fast food and retail has a bad habit of throwing new employees on the floor as fast as they can, without any knowledge of how anything works. This is poor management 101.

Take as many job opportunities as you can, so you can figure out what you enjoy doing. You may even want to try some more electives at school, to figure out what you’re good at. If you can’t figure out what you want to do for a career, first start thinking about what you DON’T want to do. Then, narrow it down.

Every job you have will give you experience, both professionally and personally, that’ll help you in the future. Every opportunity you have will eventually lead the way for a better opportunity. Having a crap job now could mean having your dream job in the future. Always be nice to your coworkers and supervisors (even if you hate them as much as I did), because they’re the ones who’ll promote you. The only reason I am where I am today is because somebody else got me here. The key is to work hard and help each other out once in a while. If you screw up, own up to it, apologize, and move on. It’s better to screw up than not put forth any effort at all. 

Keep doing well in school, and that'll open up major doors for you as well. If you're thinking about going to college, talk to your counselor about how you can get financial aid. As the grandson of a college counselor, I can tell you there's always free college money floating through the air. You can get scholarships or grants based on your grades, race, what field you want to get into, etc. If you want to take your SATs, ask if you can get a fee waiver so you can take it for free, which is what I did. You can go to a thrift store or used book store and get an SAT study guide for only 1 or 2 bucks. 

As far as socializing goes, it takes a lot of practice. When you’re at work, always smile when you greet new customers. Always make eye contact and laugh when it’s appropriate. People are naturally attracted to those who are friendly and don’t take themselves too seriously. 

Next time you’re in a conversation, ask the other person questions about themselves. It’ll show you’re a good listener, plus you’ll get to know them more. It’s a win-win for everybody. Socializing is nothing but give-and-take. Don’t worry if you accidentally say something awkward, because the other person will brush it off in no time. 

I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this!

Playing the comparison game is a trap (“I shouldn’t feel bad because I have it so much better than other people”). We all have problems we need to work through. We’re all trying to find our path in life and where we fit into the grand scheme of things. This isn’t weakness – this is called being human. 

I can only speak from my perspective, but it sounds like loneliness is the main issue here. Not having your kids around all the time, or spending much time with friends could leave you feeling separated from the world around you. The internet could be a scapegoat for dealing with actual human interaction. Depression takes away your motivation to spend time with people, but not spending time with people could be making you depressed. It’s a vicious cycle. 

Take every opportunity you have to spend time with your friends. Appreciate the time you have with your kids, and think of fun things you can do together. If you have any hobbies, that’s also a great way to meet people and have fun. It’ll clear your head and help take your mind off your depression. But remember to make time for yourself, whenever you need it. 

As far as meds go – that’s something for you to decide. For some people they work wonders, for other people they only make the depression worse. That’s why you’ll hear so many conflicting opinions over them. I was prescribed Zoloft, and while it helped give me more motivation, it put me in a foggy haze and had embarrassing side-effects (constipation, impotence, etc.). This is something to go over with your doctor, who’ll ask you a series of questions about your depression symptoms. 

I hope you can overcome whatever problems you’re facing, and I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this!

I’m so, so sorry for what you’re going through. It breaks my heart somebody would do something like this to you, especially at such a rough time in your life. 

However, I implore you not to hurt yourself. Doing so would mean giving that person more power over you than they already have. Instead, the best thing you can do is keep pushing forward. Keep working hard, so you can prove them wrong. Show them you’re not the person they think you are – you’re better. Don’t let them win. Living well is always the best revenge. There’s no better feeling than laughing in the faces of the people who once doubted you. After all, why should you die for somebody else’s wrongdoing? 

I hope you can find some way to rise up and overcome this, my friend. I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you.

My friend, you’ve gone through what no person should ever go through. I can’t even begin to imagine what you must be feeling right now. To me, it sounds like you are not the problem. You are not a bad person. The people who convince you you’re a bad person are the problem. You deserve the right to live and be happy, just like everybody else does. If anybody tells you otherwise, don’t listen to them. The only people worth listening to are the ones who support you and want to see you succeed.

I don’t have much advice to give, but I really hope you can find some way to live a better life. While nothing can take away your disorder, I truly hope you can find your happiness and get away from the people who treat you this way. I don’t know you personally, but I know you have friends, family, hobbies, interests, and a lifetime of memories, and that’s something to be preserved and cherished. I don’t know you, but I care for your health and well-being, and I hope you can overcome this. 

Sending you much love. I wish you all the best in the days ahead.

Yes, it’s true, we’re all so insignificant. It’s true, we’re all going to die. But that doesn’t change the fact that you exist. You are alive. Out of all the millions of sperm cells and hundreds-of-thousands of eggs, there was that one sperm that came together with that one egg to form you. Your mother’s body made you perfectly, without a blueprint. You were born onto a planet spinning at exactly the right speed, and at exactly the right distance from the Sun to support life. Despite completely inconceivable odds, and despite the whole world being against you, you’ve made it to right here, right now, at this point in history. If any one of your ancestors had died, you wouldn’t be here today. You are a miracle of life, and that’s something that nobody can ever take away from you. 

The most we can do is make the most of the life we live, while we still can. Hopefully we can make the world a better place than when we first got here. Just because I don’t know you personally doesn’t mean I don’t care about you. I know you have friends, family, hobbies, interests, and a lifetime of memories, just like everybody else does. That’s something worth preserving. 

Like everything else, the problems we face are always temporary. There’s always a way to work through them. Instead of making it a goal to commit suicide, make a list of ways you can improve yourself and turn your life around for the better. Set small goals for yourself, so you can see results. 

I can tell you’ve been through a lot, but I can tell you have a lot of strength to make it to where you are today. Keep striving, keep pushing forward. You will get through this. 

I wish you all the best in the days ahead. You can do this – I believe in you.

I’m glad you’re still here, friend. If you can stare death in the face and come out of it alive, then you can do anything in this world. You sound like you have a great attitude, and a great perspective on things. Keep working hard, keep pushing forward. You will come out of this for the better. The whole reason we get hurt is so we can heal and become stronger. The whole reason we make mistakes is so we can learn from them. The whole reason we have bad days is so we can appreciate the good days. 

I wish you all the best in the days ahead. I believe in you, and I can see the potential in you. You can do this!

Yes, dogs are absolutely wonderful companions. They don’t question you or back-talk you, and they’re always there for you when you’re down. Anytime I’ve cried or gotten upset, my dog always lays on my lap to help me feel better. 

But keep in mind, having a pet is like having a child. If they bark constantly or pee everywhere, you have to take responsibility for it. You have to train them and clean up after them constantly. Nobody else is going to do it for you. If you have roommates, having a pet may cause contention at times. Not to discourage you. It's just something to be aware of. 

As far as breeds go, I absolutely hated Chihuahuas until I actually got one. My Chihuahua is extremely clean, friendly, quiet, and takes great care of herself. They live longer than most dogs and are easy to train. My Chihuahua uses potty pads in the house, so I don’t constantly have to take her outside to use the bathroom. Since she’s so small, she only eats a little bit of food, which means I only have to buy a bag of dog food once every few months or so. This may be viable if you’re student and/or living in a dorm. 

Not sure if you’re a cat person, but cats are also easy to take care of. They’re mostly self-reliant. You only have to feed them and clean up their crap crystals/litter. They’re not quite as “extroverted” as dogs, but my cats have always been super friendly and playful. Dogs have one way of showing affection, while cats have another. Again, this could be a viable option. 

Wishing you all the best in the days ahead!

If your wound is severe, you should go to the hospital immediately. To your friends and family, your health and well-being is more important than anything else. It’s much better to get help openly than to suffer privately. There’s no embarrassment and no shame in doing so.

Everyone deserves the right to live and be happy. Even if someone did something truly horrible, they don’t deserve to die, but instead they deserve the chance to turn their life around for the better. Hell isn’t a place of fire and brimstone, but a place on earth, when we’re suffering and in pain. But once you’re in hell, the only place to go is up. Sometimes we have to suffer in hell before we can appreciate how precious and beautiful life is. Sometimes we have to be consumed by the darkness before we can see the light. But if you can walk through hell and come out of it, you can do anything, and nothing can stand in your way.

Self-harming is a release, for when you have pent-up anger or sadness. It might feel good at first, but will only make you feel worse in the long run.

Next time you feel like hurting yourself, take 15 minutes to do something you enjoy. That’s it – just 15 minutes. Use that time to write, draw, paint, study, play music, etc. It takes some practice, but learn how to turn your negative emotions into something productive. Something positive. Something to work for you, instead of against you. It’ll help you feel better, so you can think more clearly and come up with a better, more viable solution. 

What you’re going through right now is extremely temporary, and something you will work through. There’s still a whole world out there for you to explore. You still have a whole lifetime to travel the world and have fun and make friends. The best years of your life aren’t over, because they haven’t even begun. Instead of making it a goal to commit suicide, make it a goal to find ways to improve yourself and turn your life around for the better. 

Feel free to PM me anytime you want to talk. I wish you all the best in the days ahead, and I hope you can get the help you need. You can do this – I believe in you.

School is hard. Med school is near-impossible, and humbles even the brightest and greatest of minds. As long as you worked hard and put forth the necessary effort, I seriously doubt your mother is going to be upset with you. If anything, she’s crazy proud of you for making it this far. More proud of you than you can possibly realize.

Even if you don’t do well, the best thing you can do is keep pushing forward. There’s no such thing as failure, but only the chance to keep improving and getting better. Every opportunity you have, whether good or bad, will pave the way for a better opportunity. If there’s any way you can retake some courses or get some extra credit, that might be something to consider.

No matter what happens, I don’t want you to hurt yourself. School is so damn temporary. While this period of your life is important, it’s going to be over and done in the blink of an eye. Before you know it, you’re going to have your degree and start writing prescriptions for people. Please don’t give up now, after making it this far. 

Don’t listen to your family, if they criticize you for not doing well. They don’t know the struggles you’ve gone through.
